DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiologic Jaundice of the Newborn

The clinical picture of a 5-day-old with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (Total 7 mg/dL), low reticulocytes, and a negative Coombs test, combined with normal feeding and no signs of hemolysis or infection, strongly supports a diagnosis of physiologic jaundice. The maternal-fetal Rh incompatibility (Mother Rh-negative, Baby Rh-positive) is not causing hemolysis in this case, as evidenced by the negative Coombs test and low reticulocyte count. The bilirubin level is well within the range for physiologic jaundice in a healthy, term, exclusively breastfed infant.
